newsitem.title: TURKEY: U.S. begins fresh evacuation of Iraqi aid workers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. begins fresh evacuation of Iraqi aid workers.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday began evacuating a new group of thousands of Iraqi employees of U.S-linked aid organisations from Kurdish-held northern Iraq, Turkish border officials said.
The officials told Reuters around 250 Iraqis had crossed the Habur border gate into southeast Turkey and were being temporarily housed in a gendermarie post.
Washington has already evacuated some 2,700 Iraqi aid workers and opposition figures, mostly Kurds, in fear of Baghdad's recent increased influence in northern Iraq.
A Turkish foreign ministry spokesman said 4,500 Iraqis would be brought to Turkey in the latest evacuation and then flown to the island of Guam, a U.S. territory in the Pacific Ocean.
"The operation is expected to be completed within two weeks," spokesman Omer Akbel told a news briefing in Ankara.
Iraqi troops crossed into the Kurdish region of northern Iraq for the first time in five years in late August to aid one Kurdish militia in fighting against a rival.
Iraq's Kurds broke from Baghdad after the 1991 Gulf War under the shield of U.S.-led allied air patrols but the region has since been blighted by factional fighting.
